newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cotton complaint revives EU anti-dumping file.
newsitem.headline: Cotton complaint revives EU anti-dumping file.

text.p: The European Commission has received a revised complaint from EU cotton producers about alleged dumping of grey cotton on EU markets, raising the prospect of a new anti-dumping inquiry into the trade.
"I can confirm that we have received a complaint," a European Commission spokesman told Reuters on Thursday.
The spokesman could not say whether the complaint came from EU cotton industry association Eurocoton nor could he detail the producer countries cited or the allegations themselves.
Eurocoton, the originator of a recently failed complaint about cotton imports, was not immediately available for comment.

The complaint means Commission officials must reopen the case file on unbleached cotton imports, a file closed barely two weeks ago after EU member states rejected a Commission plan to impose duties on such imports from China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Turkey and Pakistan.

Commission officials have one month to satisfy the case for an inquiry which, if established, kicks off an inquiry lasting a further nine months to see if the application of provisional duties is justified.

It comes as several EU member states and retail and consumer organisations are questioning the fairness of EU anti-dumping rules, which they say favour producers' interests within the bloc at the expense of importers and users.
The recently rejected measures would have hit imports from the six named countries which were worth 379 million European currency units ($436 million) in 1995. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
